summary.intent: Complete the full lifecycle of Phase 72 (SDK Write-Plane Durability and Correctness) for the CipherBox monorepo — audit stale todos, plan, execute, and ship the phase — while also firefighting concurrent CI regressions and web-e2e flakiness that surfaced mid-session.
summary.outcome: Phase 72 shipped as PR #602 with all 10 plans, 6 success criteria, a HIGH-severity moveItem write-chain resurrection fix, a CAS-merge remote-deletion bug fix, a DoS cycle-guard fix, a new CI test-typecheck gate, and 3 flaky web-e2e tests fixed; two prior CI regressions (PR #600, #601) were also diagnosed and merged; all CodeRabbit/security findings resolved and PR review threads closed, with merge left to the user.

repo: `gh workflow run <file> -f ref=<branch>` returns 422 on this repo — use `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` instead (main's workflow definition predates the ref input).
`ci-e2e.yml` (web-e2e + desktop-e2e) only triggers on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PR authors must manually dispatch it against their branch to get pre-merge e2e signal.

vitest ignores `.env` files — sdk-e2e tests read `process.env.SDK_E2E_SECRET` directly with a fallback default, so it must be explicitly exported before running the suite locally, matching the API's `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET`.

`tests/web-e2e` `ciFloor()` helper only raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor under `process.env.CI` — local runs use the raw (often much shorter) caller timeout, causing local-only flakes on IPNS-gated waits that pass reliably in CI.

Root `pnpm typecheck` only ran each package's `tsconfig.build.json` (which excludes test files) plus `tsconfig.scripts.json` — test files were never typechecked in CI, allowing ~113 TS errors (vitest v2→v3 Mock migration + Phase-62 retired-type drift) to accumulate silently.

`packages/sdk` resolves `@cipherbox/*` cross-package imports via workspace symlinks to built `dist/`, not path aliases or TS project references — so a test-inclusive typecheck gate must run build-first, per-package in dependency order (crypto→core→api-client→sdk-core→sdk).

GSD executor commits use non-conventional `feat 51-03:`/`refactor sdk:` style that fails the `pr-release-preview` CI gate; must reword via `git filter-branch --msg-filter` before opening a PR (interactive rebase unavailable in this environment).
`github-actions[bot]` pushes a `chore(release)` commit after `gh pr create` and after a passing Release Preview — always fetch+rebase before the next push or it's rejected.
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL — patch PR bodies via `gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/<N> -F body=@file` instead.

`walkChildWriteKey`'s 'nullable' mode does not swallow AEAD unseal failures — they always propagate; only the missing-WriteChildRef case returns null, a subtlety that diverged from the literal RESEARCH.md wording.

code.finding: Base-aware CAS-merge for writeChildren originally only guarded against resurrecting entries deleted locally (protected against stale remote overwrite) but failed to honor concurrent remote deletions — an entry present in base+local but removed by a racing remote writer got silently resurrected. Rewritten as a symmetric 3-way prune: base-absent entries always kept (concurrent adds), base-present entries kept only if present on both local and remote.

moveItem dropped the moved child's WriteChildRef from the source folder but never threaded baseWriteChildren into updateFolderMetadataAndPublish (unlike deleteItem and restoreFromBin which were fixed in this phase) — allowing a concurrent stale republish of the source folder to resurrect write capability for an item that had been moved out, an authorization-boundary leak. Fixed by capturing sourceBaseWriteChildren before the drop filter and threading it through.

collectDescendantIpnsNames had no cycle guard (unlike its sibling dfsFindFolder which threads a visited Set) — a cyclic or malicious folder graph would cause unbounded recursion (DoS-class stack overflow/hang). Fixed by threading a visited: Set<string> marked synchronously before any await, shared by reference across recursive calls.

restoreFromBin's re-homing wrapped AEAD unseal/reseal failures inside the same fail-open catch meant only for IPNS resolve misses, silently downgrading a tampered/wrong-key write-body into a read-only restore instead of failing closed; also the source-side cleanup publish was unguarded, so a transient failure there could abort an already-durably-committed restore. Both fixed: AEAD block now has no enclosing catch (propagates), source cleanup publish wrapped in try/catch as best-effort.

workflow: When a security-reviewer and CodeRabbit CLI disagree or one 'confirms sound' logic the other flags, adversarially re-verify by hand-tracing all input combinations rather than trusting either verdict outright — this caught a real remote-deletion resurrection bug the security review had marked as sound.

For long-running background verification loops (e2e reproduction), don't repeatedly local-run under cold/loaded conditions expecting consistency — when local timeouts keep chasing a moving target (different test flaking each run), switch to running under the actual CI timeout regime (e.g. CI=1 env var) to get a representative pass/fail rather than whack-a-mole fixing individual timeouts.

Deferring non-blocking findings (style suggestions, pre-existing gaps not corroborated by multiple reviewers) as todos with file refs rather than fixing everything in scope keeps a ship cycle from stalling on low-value work — but must be captured durably (todo files), not just mentioned in chat.

Capturing a discovered-but-deferred task (e.g. the vitest v3 Mock drift + CI typecheck gap) as a pending todo file immediately, before continuing other work, prevents it from being lost across context compaction.

Running post-fix live e2e suites (not just unit tests) after high-blast-radius refactors (CAS-merge rewrite, bin-clearing helper extraction) is necessary because unit mocks can pass while real IPNS round-trip behavior regresses.
